worst_places.quote: Нет. Kafka не умеет то, что умеет RabbitMQ: приоритизация очередей, встроенный DLX, богатая маршрутизация через Exchange, RPC-паттерн с reply queue.
worst_places.problem: Four undefined terms in a single sentence (DLX, Exchange, RPC, reply queue), in a file that defines nothing at all. Article 06 is 480 words of pure comparison: it uses DLX, DLQ, RPC, SNS, SQS, MSK, prefetch count, backpressure, fanout/direct/topic/headers exchange, compact topics, vendor lock-in, source of truth, throughput, latency, replay, offset, partition and consumer group — and glosses none of them. The reader who arrives here from a search for 'Kafka or RabbitMQ' has no anchor.
worst_places.before: Нет. Kafka не умеет то, что умеет RabbitMQ: приоритизация очередей, встроенный DLX, богатая маршрутизация через Exchange, RPC-паттерн с reply queue.
worst_places.after: Нет. У RabbitMQ есть четыре вещи, которых у Kafka нет. Приоритизация очередей: срочные сообщения обгоняют обычные. Встроенный DLX (dead letter exchange) — брокер сам складывает неудачные сообщения в отдельную очередь, без кода. Богатая маршрутизация через Exchange: брокер сам решает по правилам, в какую очередь положить сообщение. RPC-паттерн с reply queue: отправитель ждёт ответ в отдельной очереди, как при обычном вызове функции.

worst_places.after:
This enables three things.

**Multiple independent consumers.** Search, Analytics, and Fraud Detection all read the same topic, and none of them affects the others.

**Replay after failure.** A service goes down for 2 hours and restarts. It reads from its last committed offset and catches up on everything it missed, with no loss.

**New services.** A new ML (machine learning) service connects and reads the full 30-day event history from the start. The producer needs no changes at all.

patterns: Article 02 is written as the zone's glossary — every Kafka noun gets a bold lead definition — and articles 03, 05, 06 and 07 then silently inherit it and define nothing of their own. 03 opens with «в какой из N партишнов топика его записать» (topic, partition, producer bare); 05 uses producer/broker/consumer/offset/acks/ISR bare; 06 and 07 use consumer group, retention, replay, throughput, at-least-once bare. The load-bearing case is `lag`: it is the punchline of a section in 03, 05 and 07, and defined in none of them (only in 04 and 08). This is the site-wide failure mode, confirmed here: a reader arriving from search into 03, 05, 06 or 07 gets no definitions at all.

Layout and density invert exactly at the interview file. Articles 01-07 hold D=5 because every new idea is immediately followed by a txt diagram — this zone's strongest asset. Article 08 (2714 RU / 2896 EN words) has one code block and zero diagrams, 25-27 over-long paragraphs and the zone's longest sentences (RU 59w, EN 68w). Because the kafka topic has no question bank and no quiz, 08 is the reader's only retrieval-practice surface and is the one file formatted as a wall.

The RU layer is not fully translated below the H1. English survives inside Russian diagrams and prose («Это bottleneck», «Faster controller failover», «event-driven retention», «Dead Letter Queue for failed messages», «discovery кластера», «network blip», «а не чистым техническим fit»), and English verbs get Russian endings («ревокают», «ревокации», «мониторится», «батчить»). Two of these are outright errors: «нефриптографическая» (03) and «ту же партишну» / «фундаментальная компромисс» (08 / 01).

EN is harder than RU wherever the flags cluster, and not only because it is longer. EN 01 has 10.9% long sentences against RU's 1.5%; EN 08 11.6% against RU's 4.3%. EN also introduces C1 vocabulary that has no RU counterpart in the same slot: 'going sideways', 'quibble', 'commodity hardware', 'headroom', 'provision', 'canonical', 'forfeits', 'spin up', 'wired directly', 'retroactively'.
notes: RU 06's H1 «Kafka vs RabbitMQ» is fine as-is (both are product names, «vs» is standard in RU tech writing) — the real untranslated layer is inside the RU diagrams, see pattern 3. Kafka/06 heavily duplicates content/topics/rabbitmq/ru|en/05-rabbitmq-vs-alternatives.md (both cover log-vs-queue, dumb/smart broker, replay, routing, cloud managed options) and the two disagree twice: rabbitmq/05 lists «Exactly-once semantics с Kafka транзакциями» as a plain Kafka strength while kafka/05 and kafka/08 insist it holds only Kafka→Kafka; and rabbitmq/05 rates RabbitMQ at «~50k–150k сообщений/сек на ноду» while kafka/06 says it «отлично справляется с сотнями тысяч сообщений в секунду». Cross-zone RU terminology also clashes: kafka uses «партишн»/«consumer», rabbitmq uses «партиция»/«потребитель» — for a reader following the cross-reference these read as different concepts. Two factual slips noticed in passing, outside the readability remit: ru/04 and en/04 call `idempotent: true` «настройка брокера» / «broker-side setting» (it is a producer client option), and ru/04:390 leaves a dead destructure `const { CONNECT, DISCONNECT, REQUEST_TIMEOUT } = consumer.events;` that the EN version already removed.
